title: Vows
lead: A vow is a promise to give God something, often made in a time of need. The Bible takes vows seriously, fixes rules for paying them (Leviticus 27; Numbers 30), and warns against rash ones (Ecclesiastes 5:4–6).

sections.b: Jacob vows a tenth at Bethel (Genesis 28:20–22). Leviticus 27 sets the values for vowing persons, animals, houses and fields, and Numbers 6 and 30 give the Nazirite vow and the rules for women's vows. Jephthah's rash vow costs his daughter (Judges 11:30–40); Hannah vows her son and keeps her word (1 Samuel 1:11, 27–28). The Psalms often promise to "pay my vows" (Psalm 116:14). Ecclesiastes warns that it is better not to vow than to vow and not pay (Ecclesiastes 5:4–6). Jesus condemns vows that dodge care for parents (Mark 7:9–13) and tells his followers to let their yes be yes (Matthew 5:33–37), yet Paul takes a vow and pays for others' Nazirite offerings (Acts 18:18; 21:23–26).
